page: Hetzner Cloud ccx43 is a dedicated CPU virtual server powered by the QEMU hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, configured with 16 virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 62.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 3.91 GB per core. Local storage is bundled as a 360 GB NVMe SSD. No GPU hardware is included, and the instance comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 3056.68 and bzip3 single-threaded decompression reaching 13.85 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% of tested servers. Multi-core and memory performance generally fall within the average range, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 24552.03 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11128.0. Memory bandwidth is measured at 52.44 GB/sec for large block reads and 37.18 GB/sec for large block writes. For LLM workloads, the server achieves a strong text generation speed of 269.05 tokens/sec on a small 135M model, but performance drops to a poor 4.17 tokens/sec for prompt processing on a large 70B model.

The ccx43 offers qualitative cost efficiency by providing dedicated AMD EPYC resources and local NVMe storage, which avoids the resource contention typical of shared-core instances. However, the lack of a GPU and the poor performance on large-scale LLM inference represent clear tradeoffs for machine learning workloads. This server is best suited for general-purpose workloads, software compilation, database operations, and static web serving.
description: Hetzner Cloud ccx43 is a dedicated CPU virtual server featuring 16 vCPUs (8 physical AMD EPYC cores at 2.0 GHz) and 62.0 GB of RAM. It includes a 360 GB local NVMe SSD and operates on the x86_64 architecture via the QEMU hypervisor. Benchmarks show strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core and single-threaded bzip3 decompression scoring in the top 25%. Multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations align with average mid-range standards. Lacking a GPU, it exhibits poor performance on large LLM inference tasks. This server is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring dedicated CPU resources without shared-host contention, making it highly suitable for software compilation, static web serving, and general-purpose database applications.
